title: Journey 2: Multi-Agent Token Economics & AST-Graph Traceability
description: Master when to keep AST-Graph lookups direct in a Frontier Root session vs. delegating to subagents, and how Context-Zero Orthogonal Validation prevents confirmation bias.

nodes.title: 1. The ~8k–15k Subagent Cold-Start Tax vs. Direct AST Span Resolution
nodes.objective: Calculate when direct AST-Graph lookups beat subagent delegation and naive 800-line file chunking.

primaryModality.questionPrompt:
### Checkpoint 2.1: Subagent Cold-Start Tax vs. AST-Direct
Use the interactive Token Crossover slider below to test **2 files** with **low log entropy (4 KB)** vs. **88 KB of noisy Playwright/build logs**:

{{WIDGET_EMBED}}

You are running on a Frontier root model (**Gemini 4 Argon** or **Claude Opus 5.5**) and need to locate a symbol definition, trace 2 callers, and edit **2 files** (with no noisy log dumps). What is the optimal execution strategy and why?
options:
Option A: Keep execution **direct in the root session** using `ast_symbol` and `ast_refs` exact line-span reads:
```python
# Avoids the ~11.5k token subagent cold-start tax & handoff loss
# Reads only pipeline.py#L142-L184 (~980 tokens total)
```
Option B: Spawn a subagent with `Model: "pro"` to grep the codebase and summarize the 2 files.
Option C: Call `read_file` in 800-line chunks (`L1-800`, `L801-1600`) across both files in the root session.

1.diagnosis: Two traps here! First, spawning a subagent for a bounded 2-file edit pays an immediate **~8k–15k token cold-start tax** (system prompt + tool schemas) for a task that only costs ~2.7k tokens directly via `ast_symbol`. Second, passing `Model: "pro"` from a Frontier root routes to a legacy preview endpoint that 404s (always use `Model: "inherit"` or `"flash"`).

2.diagnosis: Paging through files in 800-line chunks pollutes the root context window with ~22k+ tokens of irrelevant code when `ast_symbol` returns the exact `#L142-L184` span in 12ms.

remediationModality.questionPrompt:
### Remediation 2.1 (Alternative View: Token Accounting Breakdown)
Compare the exact token footprint of all three strategies for a 2-file edit vs. an 88 KB log dump:

```diff
--- Strategy_Subagent_On_2_Files (Wastes 11.5k Cold-Start Tax)
+++ Strategy_AST_Direct_On_2_Files (Optimal for 1-4 files, low noise)
- Subagent System Prompt + Tool Schemas:  11,500 tokens
- Handoff Prompt + Summary Synthesis:      1,800 tokens
+ ast_symbol + Exact Span Read (#L142-184): 2,700 tokens (Save 10,600 tokens!)
```

| Workload | Root Direct + AST | Subagent (`flash` / `inherit`) | Winner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1–4 Files, Low Noise (<10 KB)** | **~2.7k–5.4k tok** | ~13k–17k tok (incl. cold-start tax) | **Root Direct + AST** |
| **High-Entropy Logs / DOM (90 KB)** | ~28k tok (Pollutes Root!) | **~1.8k tok in Root** (25k quarantined in Flash) | **Quarantine in Flash Subagent** |

Now consider the opposite scenario: a test run fails and produces a **95 KB Playwright DOM + stack trace log**. How should a Frontier root agent handle inspecting that log?
options: Option A: Delegate log forensics to a `gemini-3.8-flash` subagent so the 95 KB (~26k tokens) of high-entropy noise is quarantined out of the root context window, returning only the compact root-cause summary.
Option B: Read the entire 95 KB log directly into the Frontier root context window in 800-line chunks.
Option C: Ignore the test failure and skip verification.

nodes.title: 2. Context-Zero Orthogonal Cross-Model Validation
nodes.objective: Understand why auditors must not inherit author chain-of-thought (Context-Zero) and why lower-tier models must never semantically critique frontier diffs.

primaryModality.questionPrompt:
### Checkpoint 2.2: Context-Zero Orthogonal Audit
Inspect the cross-model verification flow below:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Auth["Author (Gemini 4 Argon)"] -->|"Quarantine Author CoT!"| X["✗ Dropped"]
  Prompt["User Prompt + RATERS.md + git diff + ast_blast_radius"] --> Aud["Orthogonal Auditor (Opus 5.5 / Inherit)"]
```

Why must a Context-Zero validation subagent inspect **only** the User Prompt, `RATERS.md`/`AGENTS.md`, `git diff`, and `ast_blast_radius`—**without** receiving the Author agent's chain-of-thought or conversation transcript?
options: Option A: Passing the author's reasoning trace primes the auditor with confirmation bias (sycophancy), causing it to rationalize the same blind spots and miss subtle invariant violations.
Option B: `git diff` cannot be run if a conversation transcript exists.
Option C: Lower-tier Flash models require empty prompts to Critique Frontier models.

1.diagnosis: `git diff` is a filesystem/VCS operation; the issue is cognitive/attentional: when an LLM reads a persuasive chain-of-thought explaining *why* a shortcut was taken, its defect-detection rate drops from ~93% to ~41%.

2.diagnosis: Never use a lower-tier model (`flash`) to semantically critique a Frontier model (`gemini-4-argon` or `claude-opus-5.5`)—always use a peer Frontier tier (`Model: "inherit"`) with Context-Zero isolation.

remediationModality.questionPrompt:
### Remediation 2.2 (Side-by-Side Diff: Biased vs. Context-Zero Subagent Invocation)
Compare the flawed auditor invocation (which leaks author rationalizations and downgrades the model tier) against the valid Context-Zero invocation:

```diff
--- Flawed_Auditor_Call (Biased + Down-Tier Anti-Pattern)
+++ Valid_Context_Zero_Auditor_Call (Orthogonal + Clean Input)
 invoke_subagent(
   Role="Orthogonal Diff Auditor",
-  Model="flash",
-  Prompt=f"Here is my reasoning why I skipped the teardown check: {author_cot}. Looks good right?"
+  Model="inherit",
+  Prompt="Audit uncommitted `git diff` and `ast_blast_radius` against User Prompt and AGENTS.md invariants."
 )
```

When invoking an orthogonal validator from a **Gemini 4 Argon** root session in Antigravity, which `Model` argument and input payload should you pass?
options: Option A: Pass `Model: "inherit"` and provide only the User Prompt, project invariants (`AGENTS.md`/`RATERS.md`), `git diff`, and `ast_blast_radius`.
Option B: Pass `Model: "pro"` and attach the full author chain-of-thought.
Option C: Pass `Model: "flash_lite"` so it runs faster.
